scope: Canonical transaction policy for later SP-09 implementation. Existing runtime behavior is recorded separately from the decisions that later cards must implement.

normalStart.meaning: The web cap is an explicit session cap, not a claim that raw W3X food_made values have been scaled by a known ratio. Debug 10000/10000/10000 is test-only and cannot establish normal affordability.

currentBehavior.build: A pending order spends nothing. BuildingSystem.createBuilding spends the template web gold/lumber exactly once after start validation; skipCost sets costPaid false. Constructing paid buildings refund floor(cost * 0.75) once through cancelConstruction. Completed removal refunds zero.
currentBehavior.hatch: startCoopHatch removes one I006 egg before creating a timed job. It checks coop job capacity, but currently has no supply reservation or public cancellation. A blocked exit retains the job and does not consume another egg. removeEconomyBuilding drops coop jobs and inventory without returning the egg.
currentBehavior.upgradeResearchProduction: No generic action, queue, cost, time, reservation, cancellation, or research-level runtime exists yet.
currentBehavior.supply: PlayerWallet carries supplyCap/supplyUsed, initialized as 3/0, but current construction, hatch, initial units, death, and removal do not update them.

decisions.walletOwnership: Every transaction reads and mutates only the owning complete building's owner wallet. A different owner cannot satisfy cost, supply, cancellation, or receive refund effects.

build.cost: Use the current web template costGold/costLumber, not originalCost. Check at start after pending travel and eligibility validation; deduct atomically once.
build.cancel: Only a paid constructing building can be player-cancelled. Refund floor(web gold/lumber cost * 0.75) once. Pending orders have paid zero and cancel for zero. skipCost/test/item fixtures refund zero.
build.destroy: Destruction/removal gives zero gold, lumber, egg, supply, production, or research refund. It uses the existing single removal path.
build.buildTime: Use the existing template buildTimeSec as the web policy. Extracted W3X build time is unavailable, so no original-time replacement is authorized.

upgrade.eligibility: An upgrade begins only for an owned complete source building with upgradeTo, after source/target prerequisites and wallet checks. It is not a second direct building placement.
upgrade.costAndTime: Until SP-09-03 adds explicit upgrade records, target template web cost and target template buildTimeSec are the provisional web inputs. Original upgrade costs/times are unknown and must not be inferred from original build cost.
upgrade.payment: Deduct once at accepted upgrade start. A building has at most one upgrade or production/research job at a time unless a later explicit per-building capacity says otherwise.
upgrade.inProgress: Keep the source building's footprint, owner, selection, blocker, vision, combat identity, current HP, and active economy capability through progress. It continues its source capability; no target capability is activated early.
upgrade.completion: Atomically replace the capability/template data at completion. Preserve current HP ratio capped by target max HP; do not restore to full HP. If a target footprint cannot safely fit at start, reject before payment rather than move or overlap entities.
upgrade.cancel: Player cancellation restores the unchanged source state and refunds floor(upgrade web cost * 0.75) once. A destroyed upgrading building follows destruction and refunds zero.

production.queue: A building has a serial queue by default. The existing coop hatch capacity remains its explicit exception and is not changed by this contract.
production.payment: For generic production, deduct the declared web cost and reserve supply atomically when enqueue is accepted. Production cost/time must be explicit SP-09-03 data; no template construction cost may be reused as a unit cost.
production.cancel: A player cancellation returns the declared full unit cost and one reserved supply exactly once, then removes the job. A destroyed production building returns neither cost nor egg; it only clears jobs/reservations once.
production.exitWait: A completed job whose exit is blocked remains paid and supply-reserved. It must not complete again or consume a second input.

hatch.input: Each accepted hatch consumes exactly one stored I006 egg and reserves the result chicken's supply. The current capacity/time and blocked-exit retry behavior stay in force.
hatch.playerCancel: SP-09-09 must return exactly one I006 to the same coop inventory and release its one supply reservation. If no slot is available, cancellation fails without changing job, egg, or reservation; it must not drop an unowned field egg.
hatch.destroy: Coop removal destroys its stored eggs and jobs, releases their reservations, and refunds no egg. This deliberately differs from player cancellation.
hatch.simultaneous: For a same-tick cancel, destroy, and completion race, process a still-existing job only once: destroyed wins over completion; explicit cancel wins over completion only if it reaches the job first; all later operations are no-ops.

research.costAndTime: Research requires an explicit web cost, time, maximum level, and effect record from SP-09-03. Provider template construction cost is never a research cost proxy.
research.paymentAndCancel: Deduct once at accepted queue start. Player cancel refunds the full declared research cost once; provider destruction refunds zero and clears the job. No level changes before completion.
research.duplicate: One owner may reserve only one next level of a research key across all providers.

supply.mapping: W3X food_made becomes future per-template supplyProvided; W3X food_used becomes future per-unit supplyCost. The source contains examples such as h001 food_made 30, h00H 50, h015 65, h00A 3 and h009 food_used 2, but no web conversion ratio is known.
supply.webDecision: SP-09-03 must state every current playable template/unit supply value explicitly. Existing starting cap 3 and used 0 are the initial web values, and not a derivation from raw W3X food fields.
supply.reservation: available = supplyCap - supplyUsed - supplyReserved. Enqueue/hatch accepts only when available >= supplyCost, immediately increments reserved, and completion converts that reservation to used exactly once.
supply.lifecycle: Unit death/removal decrements used once. Job player-cancel or destruction decrements reserved once. Building destruction decreases its supplied cap but never deletes existing units or jobs; new production remains blocked while available is insufficient.

openSourceFacts: W3X extracted tables do not provide confirmed build/upgrade/research time or refund rules.
Original food fields establish raw values but not a valid web conversion scale.
Original h006/h00G gate state transition remains unobserved and is not a transaction rule.
Original research provider data does not establish research cost, duration, maximum level, or complete target effect semantics.
